items.title: PKR congress opens amid electoral setbacks and reformist departures
items.summary: The party is grappling with the departure of prominent reformist figures, internal dissent and poor results in Sabah, Johor and Negeri Sembilan, with another state election in Melaka looming. I think PKR is at a crossroads especially after losing people like Rafizi and now Izzah taking leave. A year later, both men resigned as MPs and left PKR.

items.title: Fadhlina urges PKR members to focus on ideas instead of exploiting religion
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 14 — Political competition should be based on ideas and the ability to offer the best solutions to the people, rather than exploiting matters of faith for political gain, said Wanita PKR chief Fadhlina Sidek. She said religious issues should be respected and should not be exploited for political gain, particularly during elections. “Do not incite people over matters of faith or exploit religion arbitrarily.

items.title: Health minister warns contractors: Show progress or risk losing MOH projects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) will not compromise on unreasonable delays in over 1,300 health facility development projects nationwide, and is prepared to terminate the contracts of contractors who fail to show convincing physical progress on-site. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said in a Facebook post today that such action is necessary to ensure planned projects are completed according to requirements so that the public can enjoy the benefits promptly, while also preventing the waste of public funds. Dzulkefly said that the MOH is also collaborating with the JKR, state governments, and utility companies to resolve issues affecting project implementation at the grassroots level.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain ahead tonight for Selangor, Perak, Johor and four other states, MetMalaysia warns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain, and strong winds expected to affect seven states until 9pm today. In a statement, MetMalaysia said the affected states are Perak (Bagan Datuk, Muallim, Hilir Perak, and Batang Padang), Terengganu, Pahang, and Johor (Mersing). A similar warning was also issued for Selangor (Sepang, Klang, Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, and Kuala Langat), Negeri Sembilan (Rembau and Port Dickson), and Melaka (Alor Gajah and Melaka Tengah).

items.title: KTMB adds 124 ETS, EMU Plus services, nearly 39,000 seats for National Day, school holidays
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) is adding 124 services with 38,944 seats for its Electric Train Service (ETS) and Electric Multiple Unit (EMU) Plus services during the upcoming National Day and school holidays. In a statement today, KTMB said 100 additional ETS services, offering 31,600 seats, would operate over 10 days from August 21 to 23, August 28 to 31, and September 4 to 6. Additionally, 24 extra EMU Plus services, offering a total of 7,344 seats, will operate on selected dates from August 21 to September 6, including an extension of services to Bandar Tasik Selatan.

items.title: Free rides are over: LRT3 Shah Alam Line passengers start paying tomorrow
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 14 — After six weeks of enjoying free fares, passengers on the Light Rail Transit 3 (LRT3) Shah Alam Line will start to pay for their rides starting tomorrow (August 15). The public transport operator also informed that passengers can check the fare rates for the Shah Alam Line via the official MyRapid website. “Rapid KL welcomes the public to continue travelling with the Shah Alam Line and make public transport an option for easier, safer and smoother daily travel,” the statement said.

items.title: ‘Extraordinarily rash’: Prosecutor says police officer deliberately chased Ipoh teen before fatal crash
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 14 — The High Court here was told today that the action of a senior police officer chasing a victim at high speed before crashing into him was described as a very dangerous act and showed “extraordinary rashness”. Deputy Public Prosecutor Afzainizam Abdul Aziz in his rebuttal said that DSP Mohd Nazri Abdul Razak’s action of chasing Muhammad Zaharif Affendi Muhd Zamrie at close range was done with the knowledge that the act could result in death. He said the accused was found not slowing down the Perodua Ativa he was driving even after passing a bump in the school area, but instead continued to follow closely before crashing into the victim at an intersection.

items.title: Chiba floods: Malaysians in Japan urged to stay alert, avoid unnecessary travel
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Malaysians in Japan are advised to avoid unnecessary travel and remain vigilant as unprecedented rainfall has triggered severe flooding and major transport disruptions across Chiba Prefecture and surrounding areas of the Kanto region. The Malaysian Embassy in Tokyo said road and rail networks had been severely disrupted, leaving thousands of travellers stranded, including an estimated 7,000 people at Narita International Airport. The embassy also advised Malaysians to refer to the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) for the latest weather updates, warnings and advisories at www.jma.go.jp/jma/indexe.html.

items.title: Heading to Sepang? Expect road closures for Sukma cycling events from Sunday until Aug 19
items.summary: “The four zones are Zone A, covering Jalan Pantai Sepang Putra-Sempadan Tumbuk; Zone B (Jalan Dengkil-Jenderam Hulu); Zone C (Jalan Jenderam-Salak); and Zone D (Jalan Salak Sepang-Sungai Pelek). He said that on August 16, 17 and 19, the routes involved included Persiaran Pantai Sepang Putra, Jalan Kampung Bagan Lalang, Jalan Bukit Bangkong-Tanjung Rhu and Jalan Tumbuk-Sempadan. Meanwhile, he said the closure on August 18 would involve more routes, including Jalan Banting-Semenyih towards Dengkil, Pekan Dengkil, Jalan Jenderam Hilir, Jalan Jenderam-Salak, Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi, Jalan Pekan Salak-Lembah Paya, Jalan Sepang Lama and Jalan Sungai Pelek.

items.title: Bentley owner wins RM900,000 payout after Kelana Jaya crash, Appeals Court rejects staged-accident claim
items.summary: A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing, Datuk Ismail Brahim and Datuk Leonard David Shim dismissed both MSIG Insurance (Malaysia) Bhd’s appeal and Inderpal Singh’s appeal, with RM50,000 in costs each. MSIG Insurance had appealed against the High Court’s decision allowing Inderpal’s claim for indemnification under the insurance policy, while Inderpal appealed against the dismissal of his claim for negligence and consequential claims for RM253,000 for loss of use and RM990,000 for loss of enjoyment of the luxury car. On Inderpal’s cross-appeal, he said the court agreed with the High Court that Inderpal had failed to prove that MSIG Insurance was negligent in carrying out the investigation and processing his insurance claim.

items.title: Zahid: Bagan Datuk has potential to become competitive, liveable town
items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who is also the Bagan Datuk Member of Parliament, said the parliamentary constituency had tremendous potential, and it was the responsibility of relevant stakeholders to ensure that every potential was translated into development that benefits the people. “I started the day in Bagan Datuk by listening to a presentation on the study report for the Bagan Datuk special area plan (RKK) with the Teluk Intan Municipal Council, Bagan Datuk District and Land Office and the consultants. “Insya-Allah, we will continue to strive for the best for Bagan Datuk,” he said.

items.title: Malaysia to prioritise safety of Myanmar refugees before repatriation, says foreign minister
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 14 — Malaysia will prioritise the safety of Myanmar refugees before repatriating them to their home country to ensure their welfare and lives are protected. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said cooperation between the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and the Home Ministry (KDN) was important to verify the refugees’ status and assess the security situation they would face upon return. Mohamad said Asean also viewed the issue of Myanmar refugees seriously and that it needed to be addressed collectively by member states.

items.title: Education minister: Pupil protection policy clarifies roles, does not burden teachers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — The School Pupil Protection Policy is not intended to place sole responsibility for pupil safety on teachers, but to establish a clearer framework defining the roles of all parties in safeguarding pupils’ safety and well-being. Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said the policy provided structured guidelines on the actions to be taken by various stakeholders when concerns arose over pupil safety and welfare. “This policy creates a clearer framework regarding who should do what when concerns arise regarding the safety and well-being of a pupil.

items.title: Sarawak plans third cloud seeding operation amid prolonged hot, dry weather
items.summary: State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said the mitigation measure was aimed at addressing prolonged hot and dry weather conditions that could affect water supply sources and worsen haze in several areas. “The main focus of OPA Series 3 will be on identified critical dam and water catchment areas, particularly those important for ensuring the continuity of water supply and maintaining dam levels. “Prolonged hot and dry weather could affect air quality, water supply sources and increase the risk of forest, peatland and open area fires.

items.title: Six-month traffic diversion begins today along Damansara-Shah Alam NKVE
items.summary: PLUS Malaysia Berhad, in a statement today, said the diversion is to facilitate the construction of a pedestrian bridge across the highway, as well as maintenance works by Pinnacle Homes AD Sdn Bhd. In this regard, PLUS advised motorists to comply with all traffic signs and instructions from PLUS personnel to ensure smooth traffic flow and the safety of all parties. PLUS also recommended that motorists plan their journeys and obtain the latest traffic information through the PLUS app, its official social media platforms, including X @plustrafik, and variable message signs at selected locations.

items.title: Flash floods hit parts of Puncak Alam after hour-long downpour (VIDEO)
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 14 — Flash floods have hit several areas in Puncak Alam following about an hour of heavy rain in the afternoon today, with about one foot of water recorded along Jalan Persiaran Puncak Alam 6. Are others in Puncak Alam ok?” “Info on flooded roads in Puncak Alam, guys.

items.title: Anwar: Govt measures help Malaysia weather West Asia crisis, sustain growth
items.summary: This helped contribute to the economy’s strong growth momentum into the second quarter of this year (2Q 2026), said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. “Reforms under the Madani Economy framework, together with proactive government measures, have helped shield the rakyat from the full impact of global supply disruptions while supporting consumption and economic growth,” Anwar said in a statement issued by the Ministry of Finance today. Anwar also emphasised that while Malaysia’s growth momentum remains resilient, the Madani Government remains mindful that the benefits of economic growth are not felt evenly across households and businesses.

items.title: PM Anwar hails stronger Q2 expansion, says govt shielded households from global inflation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today welcomed Malaysia’s stronger than expected second quarter growth, saying the 6 per cent expansion underscored the government’s efforts to shield households from global inflationary pressures. In a Facebook post, Anwar described the second quarter growth as the country’s strongest performance outside the pandemic period since 2014, despite global supply disruptions and conflict in West Asia. “This strength was made possible by the Madani government’s efforts to ensure the people’s lives were not severely affected by global inflationary pressures,” he said.

items.title: Two women in dock for allegedly duping retiree in Perak out of RM120,000 over fake tax arrears
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 14 — Two women were charged in the Magistrate’s Court here today with three counts of cheating a male retiree of about RM120,000 by falsely claiming they could help him settle his tax arrears. Noorfarah Surina Ahmad, 42, and Nurfalah Noordin, 33, pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out before Magistrate S. Punitha. The two women allegedly cheated Koay Kuang Hew, 60, by offering to help him settle his tax arrears, which actually did not exist, thereby dishonestly inducing Koay to give them the money, made in three transactions on April 10 and 14 and June 4 this year.

items.title: From FOMO to future jobs: PKR Youth motions put Gen Z outreach in focus
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 14 — Youth issues took centre stage at the 2026 National Congress of Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) today, with motions focusing on stronger engagement with Generation Z (Gen Z), jobs of the future, mental health and social wellbeing. Syahnaz Putera Mohd Yaacob, who is Perak AMK Information chief, said PKR faced challenges in winning support from younger voters, particularly Gen Z. “Make mental health and social wellbeing part of the reform agenda.

items.title: Three fight for one spot as vocational college applications surge past 67,000
items.summary: Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh said the figure was expected to exceed 68,000 when applications close at midnight tonight. He said this reflected strong interest in skills-based education, which was also reflected in the nearly 100 per cent employability rate recorded among KV graduates. He said close collaboration between the MOE and industry players ensured that the fields offered and skills acquired by KV students met job market requirements.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng rebukes Penang CM Chow, disputes claim DAP delegates endorsed Umno partnership
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 14 — Lim Guan Eng has clarified that Penang Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) decision to work with Umno in the state government was not discussed at last week’s Penang DAP delegates’ meeting. Lim said the meeting, attended by current secretary general Loke Siew Fook, focused solely on whether DAP should remain in the federal government, and not on Umno’s role in Penang. “However Chow should not presume that all Penang delegates endorsed his decision merely because no one raised it at Wednesday’s meeting when the Penang DAP delegates were focused on whether to stay or leave the Federal government in Putrajaya,” Lim said.

items.title: Illegal e-waste gets one-way ticket home as Malaysia targets 1,259 containers
items.summary: PORT KLANG, Aug 14 — The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) aims to return all 1,259 containers of illegal electronic waste (e-waste) to their countries of origin by year-end. AKPS Port Klang commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal said the operation is being conducted in three phases of integrated enforcement, involving about 8,000 metric tonnes of seized e-waste over the past two years in collaboration with the Royal Malaysian Customs Department and Port Klang Authority. He said scanning machines at Port Klang remain highly efficient in detecting illegal shipments, but human weaknesses in their operation still pose challenges.

items.title: Eighteen lives lost daily is tough to stomach, but Works Ministry data is finally pointing to the fix
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 14 — The use of the Road Accident Management System (RAMS) has enabled the Ministry of Works (KKR) to identify 99 locations where fatal accidents frequently occur or ‘blackspots’ on federal roads nationwide. Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said RAMS, developed by KKR under the MYJalan initiative, plays a role in systematically managing, analysing and displaying road accident data, including identifying locations where accidents frequently occur. “The average of almost 18 lives lost every day due to road accidents in Malaysia is a very worrying figure,” he told reporters after officiating the closing ceremony of the RAMS Expansion Course and Road Accident Data Reporting here, today.

items.title: Bukit Mertajam Hospital makes global green list, ranks among world’s top 250
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Aug 14 — Bukit Mertajam Hospital (HBM) here has made history by being ranked among the 250 greenest hospitals in the world in the World’s Greenest Hospitals 2026 ranking by Newsweek and Statista. The Ministry of Health (MOH) said the achievement recognised HBM’s commitment to implementing climate-friendly healthcare practices and environmental sustainability. MOH also congratulated the entire HBM staff and the MOH Engineering Services Division, which were instrumental in the hospital’s sustainability achievement.

items.title: Hop on, KK: BAS.MY pink buses expand eight routes, easing commutes across the city
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 14 — After four months of operation on its initial two routes, Kota Kinabalu’s new fixed-schedule BAS.MY “pink bus” service is now running across all eight routes, giving commuters more options for getting around the city and surrounding areas. The full rollout of routes S01 to S08 began last Tuesday, completing the phased introduction of the service that started on April 1 with routes S01 and S05. The first two routes have already recorded strong demand, with 194,265 passengers using the service between April 1 and August 10.

items.title: ‘Datuk Seri’ businessman claims trial to RM37.1m company funds breach of trust at Bukit Tunku bank
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — A businessman with a “Datuk Seri” title pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court today to a charge of criminal breach of trust (CBT) involving RM37.1 million in company funds, allegedly committed four years ago. Datuk Seri Zul Azmi Abu Hussin, 51, a director of Xspec Resources Sdn Bhd, was accused of misappropriating RM37,099,999.67 in company funds at a bank in Taman Tunku, Bukit Tunku here on Feb 15, 2022. Deputy public prosecutor Siti Suriatey Mohamed Yusoff applied for bail of RM500,000 with one surety, along with an additional condition that the accused surrender his passport to the court until the case is concluded.

items.title: Bukit Aman say they know how Malaysia Airlines pilot cleared KLIA checks after three-day interrogation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Police are pursuing members of a drug syndicate in Malaysia after a Malaysia Airlines pilot was arrested in Jakarta late last month with more than 26 kilogrammes of drugs in his luggage. According to Berita Harian (BH), Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the operation followed intelligence obtained after investigators interrogated the pilot over two days. Hussein said the investigation also allowed NCID to share key intelligence on international drug syndicates with relevant agencies.

items.title: Married couple plead guilty to causing death of three-month-old baby under their care in Johor
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 14 — A husband and wife were charged in the Sessions Court here today with causing the death of a three-month-old baby boy who was under their care in Masai last month. The accused, Mohd Iqbal Hassan, 36, and his wife, Norsiayana Abd Samad, 34, pleaded guilty after the charge was read to them before Judge Datuk Che Wan Zaidi Che Wan Ibrahim. According to the charge sheet, the couple, as persons having custody of Muhammad Saif Mohamad Sidiq, exposed the baby in a manner likely to cause him physical injury, resulting in his death.

items.title: ECRL Kota Bharu–Gombak service targets December 2026 launch, a month ahead of schedule
items.summary: GOMBAK, Aug 14 — The East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) Phase 1 service from Kota Bharu to Gombak is targeted to commence operations as early as December, earlier than the original schedule in January 2027. Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the target depends on the smoothness of the ongoing testing and commissioning processes, including the System Integration Testing (SIT) and Fault-Free Run (FFR), without any compromise on safety aspects. “We are trying to see how the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) can help facilitate matters related to the testing and certification processes to expedite this project without compromising safety.
